purpose: Bound the inference from a fixed word inventory to a general language ban: absence of a letter-equality pattern in a small chosen wordbook does not establish its impossibility in the language.
review_scope: Bounded exact-form primary-text search; root independently reopened both primary text URLs and confirmed the displayed forms. This is separate from facsimile collation.

entries.dating: Biblical text of ancient provenance; no precise composition date asserted.
entries.attestation: One written word in the cited electronic biblical edition.
entries.contextual_grammatical_analysis: Prefixed lamed preposition + yedid (beloved/friend) + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix -o; to/for his beloved. This analysis concerns the source word only.
provenance_limits: Pattern uses the unpointed letters: vowel and cantillation marks are omitted, no base letter added or removed.
No original manuscript or print image was collated in this bounded check.

entries.source_title: Sdei Chemed, Asifat Dinim letters alef-gimel, part 1; electronic reader section 98
entries.short_quote: ואף דידידי הג׳ בס׳ עמודי אש שם פקפק בזה
entries.dating: Late nineteenth-century rabbinic work by Chaim Hezekiah Medini; the electronic book presentation contains prefatory material dated 1891. This does not date the exact passage individually.
entries.attestation: Exact contiguous spelling in running text of a Dicta-labelled electronic edition; not a generated example.
entries.contextual_grammatical_analysis: Aramaic-derived connective d- attached to Hebrew yedidi (my friend), in a concessive clause introduced by ve-af: although my learned friend ... questioned this. Analysis is contextual, not an independently collated grammar annotation.
provenance_limits: Electronic reader section 98 is a locator; it is not asserted to be the original printed section numbering.
Original print image was not collated; electronic transcription accuracy at this token is not independently established by a facsimile.
No medieval or Talmudic attestation of this exact form was established.
Rabbinic mixed-register Hebrew is not a demonstration of ordinary Biblical Hebrew or every Aramaic variety.

claim_limits: NO Voynich word meaning, sound, glyph value, source-language selection, candidate key or native correspondence is assigned.
Neither source word is added to the fixed eight wordbooks (8W), and no registered source inventory or previous result is changed.
This is a source-language pattern-capacity counterexample, not a decipherment candidate or a new native test.
No general absence claim follows from unsuccessful searches for older attestations.
The strong Biblical ABCBCD witness and qualified late-nineteenth-century electronic ABABAB witness must retain their different evidential status.
